CNBC. LD datePublished 15 Oct 01:42 BST; dateModified 15 Oct 08:28 BST (DIFFERS - report both).
Headline: 'Tech stocks plunge as Fed rate hike fears, AI funding worries mount; ASML, SK Hynix slump'. By Lee Ying Shan and Sawdah Bhaimiya.
NOTE: CNBC frames this as Fed rate-hike fears + AI financing, NOT only AI. CNBC does NOT mention the Kospi trading halt or a Nikkei index figure - index-level detail came from the Guardian.
Asia: SK Hynix -10%+, Samsung Electronics -8.73%, LG Innotek -8.95%, Seoul Semiconductor -9.28%, Samsung SDI -6.26%. Japan: SoftBank Group -7.9%, Advantest -almost 14%, Tokyo Electron -6.45%, Renesas -8%. TSMC -1.81%.
Europe: ASML -6.6%, Infineon -9.4%, ASM International -9.6%, Nokia -5%.
Wall St Wed: Nasdaq -1.88% to 26,692.87; S&P 500 -1.11% to 7,718.94; Dow -0.09%.
Dan Ives, tech analyst, Yorkville Ives: 'Higher yields raise the cost of financing these builds, and investors are right to focus on balance sheets and contract structure, but rates are a financing question, not a demand question.' Ives says Treasury yields above 5%; calls pullback a buying opportunity. 'What would change our view is a demand signal, not a rate signal.'
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan and Intel's chief warned Monday financing could be a bigger headwind to AI expansion than chip or electricity shortages.
China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) claimed a memory-density architecture breakthrough at the weekend; memory oversupply feared as early as 2029. Elon Musk on X: China would be making 'a LOT of RAM in 2028'.
Agency tokens: Reuters.
